newsitem.title: USA: La. governor warns of possible Mississippi closure.
newsitem.headline: La. governor warns of possible Mississippi closure.

text.p: Louisiana governor Murphy J. Foster said Tuesday that he had warned large industries along the Mississippi to prepare for a possible closure to all maritime traffic because of hazardous conditions, according to a report in Wednesday's The Advocate, a Baton Rouge, Louisiana newspaper.
"There may come a point if this thing doesn't settle down for a while that we have no other choice," Foster said. "It is a possibility you need to think about. It is a last resort."
At a press conference, the governor also said he is pushing for a ban on shipment of barges carrying toxic chemicals while flood conditions exist in the Mississippi river.
A spokesmen for the governor confirmed Wednesday the report in the Advocate.
Foster said he'd asked for the U.S. Coast Guard to see if such a ban would be practical.
The call comes in the wake of an accident last week when a barge carrying toxic petro-chemicals was grounded and began spilling into the river.
